name: CA-50
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 10 points on the partisan index
Incumbent Scott Peters has a large cash advantage and no outside opposition spending
Prediction markets price a Democratic win around 95%
Republican Steve Cohen has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: Peters holds a strongly Democratic-leaning district, a decisive financial edge, and no outside spending against him, while markets price his reelection near certainty. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much closer race or significant outside spending against Peters would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott Peters, the Democratic incumbent in California's 50th District, advanced to the general election against Republican Steve Cohen. The district leans Democratic by about ten points, and Peters enters with roughly $2.6 million on hand after raising over $1.8 million this cycle. Cohen reports no fundraising, and no outside groups are spending against the incumbent.

Prediction markets give Peters about a 95% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the financial gap, all of which point to a comfortable Peters victory in November.
